configuration: The upstream case test_collisions of unittest/geometry-algorithms.cpp. The deck is the ur5 robot description vendored with the pinned source at code/pinocchio/models/example-robot-data/robots/ur_description/, an arm of six revolute joints carrying seven triangle-mesh collision objects and one box, parsed by the URDF geometry parser exactly as upstream parses its own deck. Upstream runs this case on romeo_small.urdf from the romeo_description package, which is not vendored under code/pinocchio/; the ur description is, with its collision meshes, and it is the deck the module's own upstream example uses. The SRDF that comes with that description removes the ten adjacent pairs, leaving seventeen. The configuration is read from ic/<ic>/operands.json, upstream taking it from a reference configuration romeo.srdf carries and ur5.srdf not declaring one; it was chosen so that the assertion the case makes, that no pair of this robot is in collision, holds with the closest pair 1.98e-02 m apart. Graded: the two coal transforms the case builds for every pair with toCoalTransform3s, and the transform of every object after the signature that runs the kinematics itself.
observable: the pose handed to the narrow phase for each collision pair, through the module's own SE3-to-coal conversion
default_vs_upstream: the ur5 description and its SRDF in place of romeo's, and the configuration as an initial condition in ic/ rather than a reference configuration read from the SRDF
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero number of ic/nominal/operands.json; the zeros are left as they are, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is not a perturbation of a length, an angle or a quaternion coordinate. Perturbing every nonzero component rather than one component per quantity is deliberate: on an earlier Pinocchio leaf, moving a single entry of a rotation rounded away in an output built from all nine and left dozens of observables with a spread of exactly zero, while moving all of them is still a two-ulp calibration. Here that is the nonzero coordinates of the one configuration: the free-flyer translation and quaternion of the base and the six joint angles of the arm. All 13 numbers of ic/nominal/operands.json move; none of them is zero. The worst measured spread over all 504 graded values is 1.2768e-15 absolute.
altbuild: none: the same source built at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off reproduces the -O2 -DNDEBUG result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. The graded quantities are rigid transform compositions and geometric distances between fixed shapes; Eigen fixes the evaluation order of the expressions, the loops are scalar, and coal's shape queries are closed form or an exhaustive minimum over a fixed set of features, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate. The alternative build was nevertheless run for every check of this leaf rather than assumed, because on an earlier Pinocchio leaf it was what exposed a graded buffer that was reading uninitialised memory.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned library, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead.

warrant: The graded quantity is the pose each shape is handed to the narrow phase in, as produced by toCoalTransform3s from the placement updateGeometryPlacements computed: a rotation and a translation in metres, in the model's Cartesian axes, named by the collision pair and the side of it the shape sits on, both fixed by the pair set the model enumerates. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 1.28e+00, it admits about 1.01e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this case can express is many orders of magnitude larger: handing the narrow phase the inverse transform, the parent joint's pose instead of the object's, or a rotation transposed by a row-major-to-column-major slip moves entries by order one, fifteen decades above the bound; and the upstream assertions stay active, so a wrong pose that somehow left the transform intact would still be caught by the disagreement between the pair-set query and the direct coal::collide call it is compared against. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these compositions differs by about a few units in the last place of the largest intermediate, some 1e-15 in these units, six decades inside the bound, and because the alternative build measured exactly zero. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst graded value by 1.2768e-15, using 1.275e-06 of the bound, that is 784,517 times of headroom across all 504 graded values; and every graded value scaled by 0.1 per cent, a fault far smaller than any this test can express, is rejected at 1,265,270 times the bound. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
